# Nocturne Terminal

A standalone GTK 3 / VTE terminal workspace for coding agents. Import project folders into the left sidebar; each project gets its own set of real terminal sessions, started in that folder, started with whichever agent you pick.

## Launch

Open **Nocturne Terminal** from the Linux application menu, or run:

```sh
~/.local/bin/nocturne
```

Dependencies are already present on this Fedora machine. For another Fedora installation: `sudo dnf install python3-gobject gtk3 vte291`. On Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt install python3-gi gir1.2-gtk-3.0 gir1.2-vte-2.91`.

## Build and install

```sh
python3 build.py --install
```

Builds `dist/nocturne-1.0.0-linux.tar.gz`, installs the application under `~/.local/share/nocturne`, installs PNG icons at eight sizes in the user icon theme, and refreshes desktop caches. Installation also creates an isolated OpenRouter Agent SDK environment, pinned to `openrouter-agent-sdk==0.8.0` and its compatible `openrouter==1.1.22` client. The launcher is independent of the source folder. Building requires Pillow (`python3-pillow` on Fedora), Python venv and pip; runtime requires GTK, VTE, and PyGObject. The SDK is not installed into the system Python or the gateway environment.

Generated artwork: `assets/nocturne-icon.png` and `assets/nocturne-logo.png`. Prompts are recorded in `assets/PROMPTS.md`.

## Use

- **Terminal view** is what opens first: plain terminal tabs with no projects, sidebar or agents. New tabs start in the folder Nocturne was launched from (your home folder from the app menu). **+** (right after the last tab) or Ctrl+Shift+T opens another terminal. The *Terminal | Agents* switch at the top left (or Ctrl+Shift+A) changes view. These tabs are not saved.
  - Each tab is named after its folder (or what the program running in it calls itself). A small pill after the name shows the command running there (`npm`, `ssh`, `sleep`…) or, at the prompt, the git branch. A background tab's dot turns pink when new output arrives.
  - The bar under the tabs shows the current folder as a breadcrumb (click to copy the path), its git branch, what is running, and the terminal size, with *Find*, *New here* (a terminal in the same folder) and *Open folder* (the file manager). The window subtitle follows the current tab's folder.
  - **Find** (Ctrl+Shift+F, in both views) searches the scrollback as plain text: Enter or ↑ for older matches, Shift+Enter or ↓ for newer ones, *Aa* to match case, Esc to close.
  - Ctrl+Shift+PageUp / PageDown switches tabs. The status bar lists the shortcuts.
- **Agent view** (the *Agent view* button at the top left, or Ctrl+Shift+A) is the project workspace described below: projects, Claude and Codex, the Explorer and the Git screens. Its saved agent tabs only start the first time you open it. Use the *Terminal* button or Ctrl+Shift+A to go back; both views keep running. `nocturne <folder>` and *Import project* open the Agent view directly.
- **Home** sits at the top of the sidebar and needs no project. It opens a shell in `~`, and the **+** menu adds Claude, Codex or Shell tabs there. Its sessions are not saved as a project.
- **Import project** (sidebar button, Ctrl+Shift+O, or `nocturne <folder>`) adds a folder to the project list. Projects persist at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nocturne/workspace.json` (default `~/.config/nocturne/workspace.json`), along with the last selected one.
- A newly imported project opens with no sessions. Click **+** at the right of the tab bar and choose **Nocturne Agent**, Claude, Codex or Shell, or use the Start buttons on the empty page. The badge shows how many sessions are running.
- **Nocturne Agent** (Ctrl+Shift+N) is Nocturne's own coding agent. After configuring your gateway once, open it from **+** and start typing: the terminal opens ready with a default model, without a startup picker. It reuses a resumed conversation's model; new conversations use your last `/model` selection, otherwise the first configured available route. `/model` (or `/models`) opens the live model picker only when requested; Esc cancels it. `/model <name>` switches directly. Your selection becomes the default for new sessions; `/help` lists commands and `/exit` leaves the agent. The interactive terminal has a persistent bottom composer and a scrollable conversation. Type `/` for the command menu; use arrows and Enter to select, and Esc to cancel. The `/model` picker supports search, arrows and Enter. Enter sends; Alt+Enter inserts a newline; pasted multiple lines stay together. Up/Down edits multiline prompts or recalls history. PageUp/PageDown and the mouse wheel scroll the conversation; hold Shift while dragging to select text. Tool calls appear inline with results and edit diffs; Ctrl+O expands output and impact details. Approvals appear inline with Allow once / Decline choices. Esc interrupts the running turn; follow-up messages sent while busy queue and are saved. Responses stream while the composer remains available. It can list directories, read files, make exact edits, create new files and run tests or other shell commands. Shell commands ask permission; Nocturne's guards, project-memory prompt hook, impact checks before/after edits and turn-end upkeep remain active. A pre-edit impact report is returned to the model for review before the edit can run. Explicit `/nocturne-*` skill commands load only the requested bundled skill. Claude and Codex subscriptions and settings are separate and unchanged.
  - You can also launch the same terminal interface directly with `~/.local/bin/nocturne-agent` in a project directory. `nocturne-agent --resume <session-id>` resumes a saved conversation; `/status` shows its id. The direct CLI uses your configured gateway.
  - Nocturne Agent uses the official OpenRouter Agent SDK (`openrouter-agent-sdk`) for model streaming, validated tools and agent loops. The installer creates an isolated runtime under `~/.local/share/nocturne/agent/venv`. A first SDK call runs without project tools or repository context to distinguish a concrete task from conversation. “Hi” and “can you help me code?” get a direct answer or clarification; a concrete request enables the guarded coding tools. SDK conversations continue through the existing saved history. `/model` reloads the saved gateway connection and lists the models currently served by it.
  - `/status` also shows the last turn's outcome and phase. Turn state and queued messages are saved together; resuming an interrupted session never replays unfinished tools. A conversation can be open in only one agent terminal at a time. Esc stops connection attempts, streaming, hooks and shell processes. Model requests and hooks have a 120-second limit, shell commands 60 seconds, and a turn 15 minutes. A failed mandatory check stops the turn. Pending after-edit checks are saved and retried before the next turn; interruption cleanup gets up to five seconds. Queued messages pause after an interruption or failure and continue after your next completed turn or on resume. A completed turn means the agent finished responding; it does not certify that tests passed.
  - Native conversations and the chosen model are saved privately under `~/.config/nocturne/cli/agent-sessions/` and resume with the tab. File tools stay inside the project; shell commands run as your user after confirmation and are not sandboxed. Esc or Ctrl+C stops the current turn; interrupted tool calls are not rerun automatically on restore. Shell commands have a 60-second timeout; turns pause after 40 model steps. 
  - **Context optimization.** Before every model request, a context budget clears duplicate and historical file reads, invalidates reads after commands/edits, and excerpts large reads under pressure. User requests, project instructions, impact reports, refusals and verification results are retained. The complete transcript stays saved; source files can be read again. The budget uses a conservative UTF-8 byte-based token estimate with output space reserved; if required content cannot fit, the turn stops explicitly. `/status` shows reported provider input/output/cache tokens and cost (unknown when absent), model request count and the latest context estimate. A stable session header supports cache-friendly routing when forwarded by the gateway; actual cache hits depend on the gateway/provider. Context compaction makes no additional model calls; the conversational scope check still costs one request at the start of each user turn.
- **Tabs are saved.** Each project (and Home) remembers its open tabs: their kind, name and agent conversation. Reopening Nocturne restores them when you open the project. Claude tabs resume with `claude --resume <id>`, and Codex tabs with `codex resume <id>`. Closing a tab with × forgets it there, but the conversation stays in the CLI's own history.
- **Rename a session** by double-clicking its tab, Ctrl+Shift+R, or by right-clicking the terminal and choosing *Rename session…*. The Terminal view edits the name in place in the tab and the Agent view asks for it: Enter saves, Esc cancels, and an empty name goes back to the terminal title. Renaming a Claude or Codex tab also renames the agent's own conversation, so it shows under the new name in `claude --resume` / Claude's `/resume`, or in `codex resume`. Nocturne writes the same record the CLI writes for `/rename` (a `custom-title` line in the Claude transcript, or a `session_index.jsonl` entry for Codex) and never types into a running agent. A conversation that has no first message yet takes the name when it starts.
- Claude tabs get their own session id when they start. Codex chooses its own id, so Nocturne adopts the first Codex session that starts in the same folder after the tab opens, once the first message is sent. If you start a new conversation inside an agent (`/clear`, `/new`, `/resume`), the tab still resumes the one it started with.
- Sessions are isolated per project. Each one has its own tab set and starts in its own directory, with `NOCTURNE_PROJECT` and `NOCTURNE_PROJECT_NAME` set. Switching projects leaves the other projects' sessions running in the background.
- Every tab is a normal terminal. Agents launch through your interactive shell, so PATH from `~/.bashrc` applies. When an agent exits, the tab drops to a shell in the project folder. If a CLI is missing, the tab says so and gives you a shell.
- Use the **+** menu at the right of the tab bar, or Ctrl+Shift+N / L / X / T (Nocturne / Claude / Codex / Shell), to start more sessions in the current project.
- **Notes.** The note icon at the top left, right after Terminals (Ctrl+Shift+J), opens the project's notes, Notion style. The list on the left works like the sessions list: a search box (it looks inside notes too), the open notes, then every other note of the project, latest edited first. Click one to open it as a tab; click Notes again (or Ctrl+Shift+J) to hide or show the list. Its two buttons make a **new note** or a **note from the clipboard** (paste anything you copied, then give it a title). A note is a title above free Markdown text: paste into it, edit it, and **Copy** at the bottom right copies its text back out. Notes save as you type (Ctrl+S saves now); a note left empty is not kept. Double-click a note's tab (or Ctrl+Shift+R) to rename it; right-click a tab or list row to copy its text, close it or move it to the trash. Notes are Markdown files in `~/.config/nocturne/notes/`, one folder per project, never inside the project, and open notes come back when Nocturne restarts.
- **Explorer and editor.** The file icon at the top left (Ctrl+Shift+E) opens the Explorer beside the tabs, VS Code style. Each project remembers its own Explorer and open files. Click a file to open it in an editor tab next to the terminals. Right-click for new file or folder, rename, move to trash, copy path, open a terminal in that folder, or show in the file manager. File names are colored by git status (M modified, A added, U untracked), and the tree follows changes on disk.
  - Editors highlight syntax in the Nocturne colors and handle indentation, bracket matching, find (Ctrl+F; Enter and Shift+Enter to step through matches) and undo. Ctrl+S saves. Ctrl+Shift+W closes the tab and asks first if it has unsaved changes.
  - **Problems** are underlined as you type, with the message on hover and a list in the status bar's problems button. Linters come from the project (`node_modules/.bin`, `.venv/bin`) or your shell's PATH: ESLint for JS/TS, Ruff for Python, ShellCheck for shell scripts. Nocturne also checks Python syntax and strict JSON itself. ESLint runs from the folder that holds its config.
  - **Format** (Ctrl+Shift+I, or the status bar button) uses the project's formatter: Prettier for web files, Ruff or Black for Python, rustfmt, gofmt, shfmt, clang-format. When none is installed, Nocturne re-indents strict JSON and trims trailing whitespace. **Format on save** is on by default and can be turned off in any editor's status bar; the setting applies everywhere. Formatting is one undo step and never overwrites text you typed while it ran.
  - When an agent or another program changes an open file, a clean editor reloads automatically. An editor with unsaved changes shows a notice instead (*Reload from disk* or *Keep mine*). Closing Nocturne or removing a project asks about unsaved files first.
- **Git screens.** The two icons at the top right open full-page screens for the current project. The branch icon is Git Flow (Ctrl+Shift+G) and the kraken icon is GitKraken (Ctrl+Shift+K). Click the icon again, press Esc, or use *Back to terminals* to return. Your sessions keep running in the meantime.
- **Changes** (on both screens) lists every changed file against HEAD, both staged and unstaged, plus untracked files. It shows a total (`7 files changed +6 −12`) and each file's own `+added −deleted` count. Status letters are M, A, D, R, U (untracked) and ! (conflict). Select a file to see its diff below the list. *Full diff in terminal* opens the whole diff in a tab.
- **Pushing.** A branch that was never pushed shows `↑N not published` and a **Publish** button (`git push -u origin <branch>`). After any push the dock asks *Create a pull request?*: **Create PR** or **Skip**. Both show the link to open the pull request on GitHub, and it stays on the final *Done* step.
- **Git Flow** uses plain git, so you don't need the `git-flow` extension. *Initialize* creates `develop`. In a folder that isn't a repository yet, it also runs `git init` and makes an empty first commit. *Start a branch* takes a name and makes a feature, release or hotfix branch. *In progress* lists the flow branches, with *Switch* and *Finish* for each. Finishing does `--no-ff` merges, tags releases and hotfixes, then runs `git branch -d`. *Status and branch graph* shows `git status` and a branch graph. Settings already in `gitflow.*` are kept. Init and Finish list their steps and ask before running, and nothing is pushed. Each step runs in its own tab so conflicts stay visible. These tabs are not restored on restart.
- **GitKraken** shows whether the desktop app is installed, opens the project with `gitkraken -p` (native, snap or Flathub install), and summarises the repository: branch, sync with upstream, remotes, changes and recent commits. If GitKraken is missing, it offers to install `com.axosoft.GitKraken` from Flathub for your user, then opens the project. Right-click a project for *Open in GitKraken* directly.
- **Skills** (the bolt icon at the top right, Ctrl+Shift+H) shows only the skills that ship inside Nocturne, across the whole page: pick one on the left to see what it does, how to run it (`/name` in Claude, `$name` in Codex), examples with *Copy* (switch between Claude and Codex), its full instructions, and an On/Off switch. Switched-off skills are not offered to new sessions.
  - `nocturne-init-feature` traces a flow with `file:line` evidence and saves a report in `.nocturne/reports/`. `nocturne-re-init-feature` reads the reports and the project memory back into the conversation. `nocturne-remember` saves a lasting project fact in `.nocturne/memory/` (start with `forget` to remove one). `nocturne-debugging` fixes a defect from evidence. `nocturne-impact-check` runs by itself before and after every edit, listing every place that uses the code being changed so the edit does not break it. That covers Claude's Edit and Write, Codex's patches, and code files changed by a shell command (`sed -i`, `cat > file`, scripts), which are checked right after the command. Type it after a fix to sweep the whole change and run the related tests. It parses code with tree-sitter (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, TSX, Go, Rust, Java; bundled in the app and run with Node), so names in comments and strings never count and only uses in the same language are listed. Without Node it falls back to built-in parsers for Python, JavaScript and TypeScript. `.nocturne/` is kept out of git through `.git/info/exclude`.
  - If another app (such as Atelier) put its own versions of these skills in `~/.codex/skills`, Codex sessions started by Nocturne switch them off, so Codex never picks `atelier-impact-check` instead of Nocturne's. Their files are left alone and the other app keeps working.
  - Nothing is written to your `~/.claude` or `~/.codex` settings: Claude gets the skills with `--add-dir` and `--settings`, Codex with `-c`. Codex's `$` menu only lists its own skills folder, so Nocturne adds links named `nocturne-*` to `~/.codex/skills` that point into the app; it never touches a real folder there.
  - **Nothing loads at session start.** Skills run when you type them: Claude and Codex are told not to load or pick them on their own, and a session that starts or resumes gets no added context (no skill list, no memory). Project memory is recalled before each task prompt through a memory index, like a book's table of contents and index: Nocturne keeps `.nocturne/index/CONTENTS.md` up to date (every memory entry and flow report with its summary, sections and line numbers, plus an alphabetical index of subjects), looks each prompt up in it, and loads only the entries the prompt is about, so a large memory doesn't fill the context. The conversation shows what it did, such as *Nocturne checked the memory index: 42 entries, 1 matched (redis-cache.md); loaded 0.2k of 98k chars*; the agent reads relevant omitted entries before investigating. Current user instructions take precedence over stale memory, and code claims still need verification. The project-memory hook can be disabled independently. Other automatic hooks are: the impact check before and after every edit, the session's own flow reports loaded again after a compact, at the end of a turn a session updates any report whose cited files changed, and **memory upkeep**: when your request corrects the agent or states a rule ("actually…", "always…", "we use…", "remember…"), Claude and Codex save it to project memory as part of the task. The instruction is internal and never shown in the conversation, and other tasks are left alone. They update the entry that already covers the subject instead of adding a new one, merge entries that overlap, and finish with one line such as `Memory: updated cache.md` or `Memory: no change`. Entries follow the memory standard in the `nocturne-remember` skill, and one that breaks it (no keywords, a vague description, a secret, "today" or "probably") is flagged right after it is written so it gets fixed. Switch it off with `"memory-upkeep": false` under `hooks` in `~/.config/nocturne/agent-tools.json`.
  - With the impact hook enabled, each submitted prompt tells the agent to follow Nocturne's impact reports and use `nocturne-impact-check` for a requested final sweep, avoiding implicit selection of a globally installed `atelier-impact-check`. Global skills and CLI settings are left untouched.
  - Nocturne's other built-in hooks still run in every session it starts, asking before git commits and pushes, database commands, package installs, a second dev server, or edits on protected branches. They are no longer shown on the screen; their switches, your own hook rules and protected branches are kept in `~/.config/nocturne/agent-tools.json`. Codex runs hooks only after you review them once: in a Codex tab, type `/hooks` and choose *trust all*. Until then, opening a Codex tab shows a reminder in the status bar.
  - When an agent finishes a turn in a tab you are not looking at, its tab's dot and the Agents count in the header turn pink until you open it.
- **AI Gateway** (the routing icon at the top right in Agent view) is connection setup for **Nocturne Agent**. Enter a gateway URL and gateway access key, then **Add model route** for each local model: a unique **Session model** alias, **Provider/model** and **Provider API key**. With an existing gateway, model discovery comes from that service; provider fields can stay empty and local routes are optional. **Test · uses tokens** makes a small Chat Completions request. To work with a model, open **+ → Nocturne Agent**; it starts with your default model. Use `/model` there to switch. The gateway screen has no Claude/Codex client selector.
  - For a local service, use `http://127.0.0.1:4000`. Keep the generated **Gateway access key**; put your OpenRouter or other provider key in **Provider API key**. LiteLLM model prefixes include `openrouter/`, `anthropic/`, `openai/`, `gemini/`, and `ollama_chat/`. Each model can have its own provider credential and optional **Provider base URL**. A key can also be an environment reference such as `os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, resolved by the gateway process. Coding models must support Chat Completions tool calling; compatibility varies by provider and model.
  - **Save connection and routes**, then **Install local runtime** if needed. Installation uses a separate Python virtual environment under `~/.local/share/nocturne/gateway/venv`; it adds no dependency to GTK. Opening **Nocturne Agent** starts the configured local service in a transient **AI Gateway** terminal if it is stopped; nothing starts before you open the Agent view and request a session. You can also use **Start local gateway** to open that server terminal explicitly. Ctrl+C in the gateway terminal stops it. The local service binds only to localhost. Restart it after changing provider routes. Remote gateways require HTTPS. Existing gateways must expose authenticated `/v1/models` and streaming `/v1/responses` endpoints for the Agent SDK. The connection test verifies a small Responses request.
  - Credentials are stored in private (0600) files beside `workspace.json`: `gateway.json` and the generated `gateway-server.json`. They are local plaintext secrets, not included in the application bundle or workspace session records. Provider keys stay with the gateway. Model usage is billed by the configured providers, separately from Claude/Codex subscriptions. Native sessions use the model you choose without automatic fallback. Durable budgets, per-project usage attribution, and team virtual keys require a separately configured LiteLLM database/service. Older Claude/Codex gateway tabs still resume using their original routes; missing routes stay saved and can be reopened with **Resume saved gateway sessions** after repair.
- Right-click a project to start a session, open the folder, rename it, or remove it from the list (files on disk are never touched).
- Copy and paste: Ctrl+C copies when text is selected and otherwise interrupts as usual. Ctrl+V pastes text; with no text on the clipboard it passes through, so Claude's image paste still works. Ctrl+Shift+C / V always copy and paste. Right-click opens Copy / Paste / Select all.
- Claude and Codex capture the mouse, so hold **Shift while dragging** to select text inside them.
- Ctrl+Shift+W closes a session after confirmation. Ctrl+Shift+PageUp / PageDown switches projects.
- **Agent view header and tabs.** At the top left, icons only: **☰** shows or hides the projects list, **⌂** goes to the Terminal view, then the four groups, each with its count: **Explorer** (open files), **Agents** (Nocturne Agent, Claude, Codex), **Terminals** (shells and git tabs) and **Notes**. The tab row shows only the group you pick, so files, agents and shells never mix. Choosing Explorer also opens the file tree; click it again to hide or show the tree (or Ctrl+Shift+E), and opening a file switches to Explorer. Choosing Agents opens the **sessions list** on the left: a search box, the open agent tabs (the most recently active first: the one you last opened, or whose turn just ended, is on top), and the Claude and Codex conversations you had in this folder before (newest first; click one to resume it in a new tab). While the list is open, the tab row shows only the active session, and picking another one in the list takes its place (the others keep running). Click Agents again to hide or show the list; without it, every agent tab is shown. Click a tab to switch, double-click to rename (agents rename their Claude / Codex session), × or middle-click to close, and **+** right after the last tab to start a new session. An empty group shows a page that offers to start one.
- The plain Terminal view keeps ordinary tabs: click to switch, double-click to rename, middle-click to close.
- **Appearance.** Nocturne follows your desktop: switch GNOME's Appearance between Light and Dark, or change the interface or monospace font in Settings (or GNOME Tweaks), and the open window updates right away, terminals and editors included. Terminals and editors use the system monospace font; interface text scales with the system font size.
- **Logs.** Nocturne writes `~/.local/state/nocturne/nocturne.log`: startup, errors, GTK warnings, every git command it runs, and any time the window stops responding for more than 2 seconds, with the code it was stuck in. Attach it, or the lines around the time, when you report a problem.

To open agents automatically for new projects, list them in `DEFAULT_SESSIONS`; agents are defined in `AGENTS`, both at the top of `nocturne.py`.

## Validation

`python3 -m py_compile nocturne.py` checks syntax. `python3 check.py` runs a GUI integration check against temporary projects and a temporary workspace file. It covers the skills and hooks (launch flags, Codex links, the hook script's guards and rules, that nothing loads at session start, the impact check before and after Claude edits, Codex patches and shell edits, the compact reload and report upkeep, Codex approvals, turn-end marks), project import and de-duplication, projects opening empty, per-project terminal isolation (each shell's `$PWD`), real PTY output, and persistence. Run it from a desktop session; it briefly opens a test window.

Terminal backend API: [VTE documentation](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/vte/gtk3/class.Terminal.html).

## Remove

Delete `~/.local/share/nocturne`, `~/.local/bin/nocturne`, `~/.local/bin/nocturne-agent`, and `~/.local/share/applications/io.nocturne.Terminal.desktop`; remove `io.nocturne.Terminal.png` from the size directories under `~/.local/share/icons/hicolor`. The project directory can also be deleted. Your project list and skill settings remain in `~/.config/nocturne` until you delete them. Delete the `nocturne-*` links in `~/.codex/skills` (they stop working once the app is gone, and Codex skips them).
